bull.b: Sustained revenue scale and material margin expansion signal durable operational improvement. Growing revenue base plus improving net margin increases reinvestment capacity, supports R&D and commercial spend, and strengthens long-term earnings power even without rapid top-line acceleration.

Outperformance in EP reflects durable competitive advantages: leading product platforms, mapping footprint and PFA leadership. Structural adoption of catheter-based ablation and mapping supports repeatable procedure volumes and long-term consumable pull-through.

bull.t: Robust cash generation and disciplined capital allocation
bull.b: High absolute FCF provides flexibility to fund buybacks, strategic investments and M&A while supporting operations. Strong cash conversion enables shareholder returns without sacrificing commercial investments, reinforcing balance sheet resilience and long-term strategic optionality.

bear.b: Although leverage ratios have improved, a large absolute debt stock limits flexibility if macro funding costs rise or cash flow softens. Material debt increases refinancing and interest-rate risk and can constrain capital allocation during industry downturns.

bear.t: Margin pressure from tariffs, inventory and product issues
bear.b: Gross-margin contraction driven by tariffs, inventory charges and product discontinuation reflects execution and product-safety risks. If such headwinds persist, they can erode operating leverage, compress free cash flow and force trade-offs between investment and margin recovery over multiple quarters.

A key diversified franchise showing near-flat growth reduces portfolio resilience. Persistent weakness in stone management and sacral neuromodulation can depress aggregate organic growth and requires sustained product or commercial fixes to restore contribution to company-wide revenue.
